newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie fights for European seat.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie fights for European seat.

text.p: France on Wednesday stripped ex-businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie of his seat in the European Parliament, but his lawyers immediately appealed against the unprecedented decision.

A decree published in the official gazette and signed by Prime Minister Alain Juppe and the ministers for justice, foreign affairs and European affairs said: "The ineligibility of Mr Bernard Tapie puts an end to his mandates as a representative of the European Parliament".

Tapie's lawyer Frederic Thiriez said such a decision by national authorities was unprecedented in the European Parliament and he appealed to the Council of State, France's highest administrative court, to suspend it.
The decree was sent to the speaker of the Strasbourg-based parliament and France's envoy to the institution will officially notify the speaker's office on Thursday.
A parliamentary committee was due to meet later this week to rule on the decree. It has the power to overturn the decision, but French officials said this was unlikely.

Tapie has already been ejected from the French National Assembly (lower house) under a court ruling, upheld by the supreme court, declaring him to be bankrupt and ineligible for public office. French authorities say he must give up his European seat for the same reason.
They say that under European Union law, individual member states determine eligibility for the European Parliament.
Thiriez said it would take a few weeks for the Counciul of State to rule on Tapie's appeal.

Tapie's lawyers have already appealed to the European Court of Human Rights that depriving him of his seat was contrary to the European Convention of Human Rights. The Strasbourg-based court usually takes several years to deliver rulings.

Tapie, the target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now-destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team he once ran, has been sentenced to jail terms of eight and six months for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match.
He is appealing in both cases to the supreme court.
